title: 1. Identify which state feedback the qualified expert needs
hypothesis: The qualified PPO checkpoint relies on changing pen-state observations to maintain sustained axial-roll success when hand proprioception and action history remain available.

prediction.against: the unmodified qualified D-036 PPO expert on the same 40 cases (seed 4140), its own process
prediction.rationale: pen_state_clamped minus expert, sustained success under the frozen D-034 reducer, paired over 40 cases; a decrease of at least 0.30 with the paired interval below zero. Each failure is split into drop versus tail-spin failure from the per-step traces. Conclusions are limited to this checkpoint's dependence under clamping (a distribution-shift intervention), not information-theoretic necessity or the sufficiency of pen-state feedback.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study feedback_lesions'
code_changes: Add --study feedback_lesions to scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py (config block feedback_lesions in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml: seed 4140, 40 cases, the frozen D-036 checkpoint and its sha256), reusing the R-041 driver/child structure: one fresh Isaac process per arm on the identical manifest.

Arms: expert, expert_repeat (reproducibility control), pen_state_clamped (every pen-state observation slice: object position, rotation, linear and angular velocity and any goal-relative pen terms, held at the case's reset-observation values before inference; the quaternion stays a valid unit quaternion), hand_state_clamped (hand_dof_pos and hand velocity slices held likewise). Action history and the simulator are unmodified.
Freeze config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_lesion_s4140.yaml before any rollout. Gate interpretation on zero expert/expert_repeat sustained flips and at most 4/40 diverged trajectories.

Report per arm: sustained successes, drops (episode ended by a fall), tail-spin failures (completed but the final-60-step predicate failed), median fall step; paired differences versus expert with t intervals.
Document that D-037 removed all feedback through action replay, whereas this intervention retains the policy and the other feedback channels.

falsified_by: The paired interval of pen_state_clamped minus expert success lies entirely above -0.30. An interval including zero establishes no difference.

approval.note: I accept the implementer's reset-value clamping definition and the revised drop-versus-tail-spin reporting, which localizes feedback dependence beyond D-037's removal of all feedback. Approve scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py with config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml for 160 episodes and zero LLM

controls.baseline: unmodified D-036 PPO expert on the same 40 cases (seed 4140), own process; expert_repeat reproduces it exactly

result.notes: Pen-state clamp: 39/40 -> 0/40, paired -0.975 [-1.026,-0.924]; 39 drops (median fall step 49, mean length 68) and 1 tail-spin failure, roll rate halves (17.0 -> 8.2 rad/s) and transverse rate rises (2.8 -> 4.6). The prediction (decrease >= 0.30) holds. Hand-state clamp (joint positions/velocities and fingertip poses/velocities) is almost as destructive: 1/40, paired -0.950 [-1.021,-0.879], but with a different failure mix: 22 drops (median step 52.5) and 17 tail-spin failures (completed but the tail predicate failed), so hand proprioception carries most of what keeps the spin rate up while pen state carries what keeps the pen in the hand. Because both lesions destroy success, this does not single out pen state; and clamping is a distribution-shift intervention, so the result is this checkpoint's dependence, not information-theoretic necessity. Reproducibility: expert vs expert_repeat identical (0 flips, 0 diverged). Pen-state failures by step ~50 match D-037's replay falls (median 49).

verdicts.reasoning: Pen-state clamped minus the unmodified expert is -0.975 [-1.026,-0.924] over 40 paired cases, below the predicted -0.30 with the interval far from it; the reproducibility control is exact (0 flips, 0 diverged). Within the narrowed hypothesis (this checkpoint, under clamping, with hand proprioception and action history live) the prediction is supported. Two limits: the hand-state clamp is nearly as destructive (-0.950 [-1.021,-0.879]), so pen state is not uniquely required; and clamping shifts the input distribution, so this is dependence, not necessity. The failure split is informative: pen clamps produce early drops (39/40, median step 49, matching D-037's replay falls), hand clamps split into drops (22) and completed-but-slow spins (17).
verdicts.next_experiment: A symbolic controller needs both pen-state retention feedback and proprioceptive spin feedback; next, measure whether generated controllers on Stage 1/2 (non-zero base rate) improve when the prompt states this two-channel requirement.

verdicts.reasoning: The named expert control was measured, and the reproducibility gate passed with zero outcome flips and zero diverged trajectories [logs/pen_spin/r044_feedback_lesions/summary.json]. Pen-state clamping reduced sustained success from 39/40 to 0/40; paired_success_difference was -0.975 with a 95% interval of [-1.026, -0.924], entirely below both zero and the predicted -0.30 threshold [logs/pen_spin/r044_feedback_lesions/summary.json]. Failures under pen-state clamping comprised 39 drops and one completed tail-spin failure, with median fall step 49 [logs/pen_spin/r044_feedback_lesions/pen_state_clamped.json]. Hand-state clamping also sharply reduced success, but the differing failure mixes do not establish distinct retention-versus-spin roles for the observation channels [logs/pen_spin/r044_feedback_lesions/summary.json]. The supported conclusion is this checkpoint's dependence on changing pen-state observations under reset-value clamping, not information-theoretic necessity or pen-state feedback sufficiency [logs/pen_spin/r044_feedback_lesions/summary.json].

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This cheaply localizes the qualified checkpoint's dependence on feedback channels, unlike D-037's removal of all feedback. However, clamping creates distribution shift, and sustained-success loss does not distinguish dropping the pen from failing the spin threshold. Narrow the hypothesis rather than interpreting this intervention as proof that pen-state information is necessary for retention; the budget remains 160 episodes and zero LLM calls.

Reuse scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml on seed 4140. Use existing per-step traces to separate drops from tail-spin failures, and explicitly limit conclusions to this checkpoint's dependence under clamping—not information-theoretic necessity or feedback sufficiency.

Implementation note: clamp = hold the named observation slice at its value from the case's reset observation for the whole episode, each arm one fresh Isaac process (D-034/D-035), cases from seed 4140 (unused).
